# Visual reference screenshots

The English/Polish files in `firefox/` are reviewed captures of `https://event-driven.io/en/` and `/pl/` from 2026-10-11, using Playwright 1.64.0 Firefox on Linux at 1440×900. The owner authorized current production as the baseline. They fix the use of historical Chromium images for Firefox comparisons; the pre-change Git build reproduced those failures, and the shared-header refactor produced zero homepage pixel differences. These production images retain the deployed control fonts; local controls now inherit Open Sans as requested. The reviewed production/local differences are 0.197% EN and 0.245% PL. The 3% tolerance is unchanged. Evidence and the reference decision are in [the header visual review](../../../docs/header-visual-review.md).

The unnamed default Chromium run keeps the existing paths in this directory. `--browser firefox` uses `firefox/` through Playwright's native optional project-name template. Explicitly named browser runs require their own reviewed images; normal tests fail on missing references.

These PNGs began as captures from `https://event-driven.io` on 2026-09-24. The category and English/Polish homepage images remain production references. The archive image was refreshed after its H1 was moved below the header, then reviewed and refreshed on 2026-10-04 from the CI screenshot after importing the newer Netflix article. The failed comparison showed the old Vertical Slices cover/title versus the new Netflix cover/title; header placement, archive layout and image sizing were unchanged. On 2026-10-05 the archive reference was reviewed again for the imported Open Source article: its cover, title, publication date and excerpt replace the Netflix entry. The header also includes the previously approved social-link cleanup. The 3% comparison threshold is unchanged. The article-footer and related-reading images are reviewed local-build references: the author query was corrected on 2026-09-28, the related section was redesigned using existing category cards on 2026-09-29, and it was moved after the newsletter signup on 2026-10-01. Viewport captures use 1440×900 on desktop and 390×844 on mobile; `article-footer-desktop.png` captures only the author section because external newsletter and comment embeds make a full-footer viewport capture unstable. They are visual benchmarks, not a claim that every detail of the old design is final.

`article-footer-production-legacy.png` and `article-reading-production-legacy.png` are diagnostic captures from the production article `/en/vertical-slices-and-dependencies/` on 2026-09-28. Production itself showed a different full article inside the author block because the old `/author/` query also matched a post slug containing `authorities`. These two captures document the old state; the visual test compares against the corrected `article-footer-desktop.png`, not the broken production capture.

Normal tests compare a locally served build (or `VISUAL_BASE_URL`) with these files and never contact production. To review the current screenshots and differences, run `npm run test:visual` and open the Playwright report with `npm exec -- playwright show-report visual-artifacts/report`. Failed comparisons retain expected, actual and diff images and traces under `visual-artifacts/results/`. CI uploads that directory as an artifact.

Only after reviewing an intentional visual or content change, regenerate the baselines with `npm run test:visual:update` against the local build, inspect the PNG diff, and commit it. To capture production again, set `VISUAL_BASE_URL=https://event-driven.io` when running the update command. Do not update screenshots just to silence a regression.

To refresh only the two Firefox homepage references after reviewing production, run `VISUAL_BASE_URL=https://event-driven.io npm run test:visual:update -- navigation.spec.ts --browser firefox --grep 'homepage renders'`. Then rerun the same selection without the update flag or `VISUAL_BASE_URL` against the local build. This leaves Chromium references unchanged.

For a new article that changes the first archive card, review the archive test’s actual screenshot and diff in the Playwright report, then update only that reference with `ARCHIVE_SNAPSHOT_SLUG=open-source-a-relict-a-charity-or npm run test:visual:update:archive` (replace the slug with the article you reviewed). Rerun `npm run test:visual` without the update flag afterward; keep all other baselines and the 3% tolerance unchanged. Client-navigation assertions wait for Gatsby Head metadata as well as the URL, because these updates commit separately.

Archive updates require `ARCHIVE_SNAPSHOT_SLUG` even when running the broad update command. The test checks that the first card links to that exact article before writing the reference. Imports and CI never enable snapshot updates.

Playwright Test manages browser/context cleanup and local server startup. Its native screenshot assertion uses the existing PNG paths, requires identical dimensions, and preserves the pixel colour threshold of 0.2 and maximum differing-pixel ratio of 0.03. Normal runs use `updateSnapshots: none`, including missing baselines. Focus tests with `--grep` rather than Vitest’s `-t`.
